exposure: Pre-induction with misoprostol vaginal insert (MVI) 200 μg
Pre-induction with Foley catheter (20 F, 60 mL balloon)
outcome: Need for oxytocin in labor induction/augmentation
Mode of delivery (cesarean section, vacuum extraction)
cohort: 503 full-term pregnant women with an unripe cervix (Bishop score < 7) undergoing labor induction (135 pre-induced with MVI and 368 pre-induced with Foley catheter)
finding: While both methods resulted in similar neonatal outcomes, pre-induction with misoprostol vaginal insert (MVI) was associated with a lower need for oxytocin augmentation and a higher likelihood of cesarean section or vacuum extraction delivery compared to Foley catheter.
mod_finding: Patients pre-induced with MVI had a greater chance of having a delivery by CS or VE compared to the Foley catheter.
